headline: GHRH and GHRP
punch: And why one of them is not a somatostatin blocker.

headline: Start with a correction
body: So the framing you will see repeated constantly is that GHRPs like ipamorelin and GHRP-2 work by lowering somatostatin. That is not what the field concluded when it worked out what these compounds actually were. | The finding was that **they were not surrogates of GHRH, nor were they acting through the modulation of the release of either GHRH or somatostatin**. They do something else entirely, through a receptor nobody knew existed when the compounds were first made.

headline: They have their own receptor
body: Cloning the GHS receptor, and then finding its natural ligand ghrelin, showed this was a separate physiological system for controlling growth hormone rather than a chemical trick that borrows an existing one. | As the review puts it, **the dual control of GH secretion became a trinity**. GHRH, somatostatin, and ghrelin. Three inputs into one pituitary, not two, and the third one had been running the whole time without anyone knowing.

headline: So what does each one do?
body: *GHRH* drives pulse amplitude through a Gs and cAMP pathway. *Ghrelin and the GHRPs* add amplitude through a completely separate Gq and PLC pathway at the pituitary. Different receptors, different G proteins, different second messengers. | And *somatostatin* gates both of them. So the correct mental model is two accelerators on genuinely separate wiring, with one brake sitting across the whole thing.
punch: Different wiring is why they add up.

headline: Why together they are
body: The review states it plainly: GHS given together with GHRH exert a **synergistic action**, and that combined administration is **the most potent GH releaser to date**. Not additive. Synergistic, because the pathways are separate. | It became the gold standard clinical test of GH reserve, and the GH it elicits is **not altered by gender, adiposity, or age**, which is remarkable given that every other GH stimulus is heavily confounded by all three.
punch: _The strongest known way to make a pituitary release GH._

headline: There is a real caveat
body: Ghrelin does oppose somatostatin's effect on GHRH neurons centrally, in the hypothalamus, which is why the somatostatin story keeps attaching itself to these compounds. That part is supported. | But the stronger claim, that the GHS receptor locally antagonises somatostatin at the pituitary itself, comes from work in pancreatic beta cells regulating insulin and has not been shown in somatotrophs. That one is an extrapolation and should be labelled as one.
punch: Partly true centrally. Unproven at the pituitary.

headline: Do they wear out at the same rate?
body: This asymmetry decides how any stack behaves over time and it is the most practically useful thing in this post. Fourteen days of continuous GHRH infusion **did not desensitise** the pituitary at all. | Twenty-four hours of continuous GHRP infusion **attenuated** the response to a subsequent bolus. So the ghrelin receptor is the part that fatigues and the GHRH receptor is not, which makes GHS-R1a the rate-limiting component of any combination.
punch: ==GHS-R1a is the rate-limiting receptor, not GHRH-R.==

headline: Which matches
body: Put that receptor finding next to the human data from the secretagogue post and they agree exactly. Thirty days of continuous GHRP-2 drove GH **more than 3 fold on day 1** and **more than 1.8 fold by day 14 and 30**. | Still working, visibly smaller, and the fade stabilising rather than continuing to fall. Same shape as the receptor kinetics predict. The ghrelin arm fades and the GHRH arm does not.
punch: The fade has a receptor behind it.

headline: Both are still gated
body: Whatever pathway a compound uses, GHRP efficacy is still gated by somatostatin tone rather than being independent of it. Glucose, free fatty acids, glucocorticoids and exogenous GH all blunt it, which is a wide range of everyday inputs. | So the three inputs are not three separate levers you can pull in any combination. Two of them run through a door that the third one controls, and no amount of dosing gets you past a closed door.

headline: What actually follows
body: Two accelerators on genuinely different wiring do multiply rather than overlap, and that is the best-supported claim here by some distance. One of them fatigues within a day of continuous exposure and the other does not fatigue in two weeks. | And both of them answer to somatostatin, which is why the timing of a pulse ends up mattering more than the size of the dose you put into it.
punch: ==Different pathways multiply. The brake still decides.==
